guides.title: Phone won't pair with the car
guides.summary: The car doesn't appear on the phone, pairing fails, or a new phone won't connect.
symptoms: phone won't pair with the car
car name not showing in the bluetooth list
new phone won't connect to the car
can't find the car on my phone

steps.text: Open Bluetooth or Phone settings on the car's screen and choose 'Add device' or 'Pair new phone'.
steps.detail: Most cars only accept a new phone while this screen is open, and only when the car is standing still (some only in Park or with the handbrake on).

steps.text: On the phone, switch Bluetooth off and on, search again and pick the car's name.
steps.detail: Keep the phone near the screen, and switch off battery saver and airplane mode.

steps.text: Check that the code is the same on both screens and accept on both, including 'Allow access to contacts' if asked.
steps.detail: If you wait too long, pairing times out. Start again from the car's 'Add device' screen.

steps.text: Delete the car from the phone's Bluetooth list and the phone from the car's list, then pair again.
steps.detail: An old pairing is the most common cause. Many cars remember only 5 to 10 phones, so delete phones you no longer use.

steps.text: Restart both: switch the phone off and on; switch the car off, lock it, wait 5 minutes and start again.
steps.detail: This resets the car's media system. Switch off Bluetooth on other phones in the car while you pair, so they don't take the connection.

steps.text: Try pairing another phone. If that works, update your phone's software and reset its network settings, then pair again.
steps.detail: Resetting network settings also forgets saved Wi-Fi networks and other Bluetooth devices.

escalate.text: The car's Bluetooth may need a software update or a check at the service centre.
tell_service: Your phone model and its software version
Whether any other phone pairs with the car
Any message on the car's screen (a photo helps)

guides.title: Phone doesn't reconnect when I start the car
guides.summary: You have to connect Bluetooth by hand every time, or the car connects to someone else's phone.
symptoms: phone doesn't connect automatically when I start the car
have to connect bluetooth every time
car connects to my wife's phone instead of mine
har baar bluetooth connect karna padta hai

steps.text: Keep the phone's Bluetooth on and unlock the phone once when you start the car.
steps.detail: Battery saver can switch Bluetooth off, and some phones stop background connections after a long time locked.

steps.text: In the car's list of phones, make your phone the preferred or priority phone.
steps.detail: With two phones paired, the car connects to the priority phone or to the one used last.

steps.text: On the phone, open the car's Bluetooth settings and allow both calls and media audio.
steps.detail: If only one is allowed, the car may not treat the phone as connected.

steps.text: Let Bluetooth run without battery restrictions (Android: battery settings for the Bluetooth app).
steps.detail: Some phones close background connections to save battery.

steps.text: Delete the pairing on both the phone and the car, then pair again.

escalate.text: The car may need a media system software update.
tell_service: Your phone model and software version
How long after starting the car you waited
Whether other phones reconnect by themselves

guides.title: Bluetooth keeps disconnecting
guides.summary: The connection drops while driving, calls cut, or music stops and starts.
symptoms: bluetooth baar baar disconnect ho raha hai
phone disconnects from the car randomly

steps.text: Move the phone out of metal holders and closed compartments; try it on the dashboard or in a door pocket.
steps.detail: Metal and some wireless chargers weaken the Bluetooth signal.

steps.text: Disconnect other Bluetooth devices from the phone: smartwatch, earbuds, a second car.
steps.detail: The phone can hand the sound to a watch or earbuds and drop the car.

steps.text: Switch off battery saver and let Bluetooth run without battery restrictions.
When does it drop?

options.label: When I plug in a USB cable

steps.text: That's normal: when you plug in, Android Auto or CarPlay takes over the phone. Calls and music then go through Android Auto or CarPlay instead of Bluetooth.
Update the phone's software, then delete and redo the pairing.

escalate.text: The car's Bluetooth module may need a check or a software update.
tell_service: How often it drops and for how long
Whether it also happens with another phone
Your phone model and software version

guides.title: Callers can't hear me, or I can't hear them
guides.summary: No sound in calls, low voice, echo, or the microphone doesn't pick you up.
symptoms: microphone not working in the car
call mein awaaz nahi aa rahi
other person can't hear me on bluetooth

steps.text: What is the problem?

options.label: They can't hear me, or hear an echo

steps.text: Close the windows, turn the fan down, and speak towards the microphone (usually in the roof near the cabin light).
steps.detail: Wind and fan noise are the most common causes of poor call quality.

steps.text: Check that nothing covers the microphone (a dashcam, a sunglasses holder) and that the call isn't muted on the car's screen.
During a call, choose the car as the audio output on the phone, not the phone itself or earbuds.
Turn the volume up during the call.
steps.detail: In most cars call volume is set separately from music volume.

steps.text: During a call, check the phone sends the sound to the car, and no earbuds or watch are connected.
Delete and redo the pairing, and update the phone's software.

escalate.text: The microphone or the car's phone module may need a check.
tell_service: Which way the problem goes: they can't hear you, or you can't hear them
Whether it happens on every call or only some
Whether it also happens with another phone

guides.title: Contacts or call history not showing
guides.summary: The car's phonebook is empty, names don't show for calls, or recent calls are missing.
symptoms: contacts not showing in the car
names not showing when someone calls
car shows numbers instead of names

steps.text: Allow the car to use your contacts: on Android, open the car's Bluetooth settings and turn on 'Contacts and call history'; on iPhone, Settings > Bluetooth > the car's (i) > Sync Contacts.
Wait a few minutes after connecting.
steps.detail: Large phonebooks take time to download, and some cars load contacts only when parked.

steps.text: Look for a 'Download contacts' or 'Sync' button in the car's phone menu, and check it isn't showing favourites only.
Save the contacts in the phone's own contacts app.
steps.detail: Contacts that exist only in a messaging app or a work account may not be shared with the car.

steps.text: Delete and redo the pairing, and accept contact access when the phone asks.

escalate.text: The car's phone module may need a software update.
tell_service: Your phone model and software version
Whether contacts appear for another phone
